Let  

\[
A=\text{“roll is 1 or 2’’},\qquad B=\text{“roll is 3 or 4’’},\qquad C=\text{“roll is 5 or 6’’}.
\]

Each roll is equally likely to be \(A,B,\) or \(C\); therefore  

\[
P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\frac13 .
\]

We stop the experiment the first time a \(C\) occurs.  
We want the probability that before this first \(C\) we have seen **at least two \(A\)’s and at least two \(B\)’s**.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.   Reducing to a two‑category problem  

Let  

\[
N=\text{number of rolls that are not }C\text{ before the first }C.
\]

Because the probability of a non‑\(C\) on each trial is \(\frac23\) and the
probability of a \(C\) is \(\frac13\),

\[
P(N=k)=\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^{k}\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr),\qquad k=0,1,2,\dots
\]

Conditional on \(N=k\), each of those \(k\) non‑\(C\) outcomes is equally likely to be
\(A\) or \(B\) (probability \(\tfrac12\) each), and they are independent.

Thus, given \(N=k\),

\[
\#A\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(k,\tfrac12),\qquad\#B=k-\#A .
\]

The event we need can only happen when \(k\ge 4\).  For a fixed \(k\ge4\),

\[
P(\text{success}\mid N=k)=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{i=2}^{k-2}\binom{k}{i}}{2^{\,k}}
   =\frac{2^{k}-(1+k+k+1)}{2^{k}}
   =\frac{2^{k}-2k-2}{2^{k}} .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.   Summing over all possible \(k\)

\[
\begin{aligned}
P(\text{success})
&=\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}P(N=k)\,P(\text{success}\mid N=k)\\[2mm]
&=\frac13\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^{k}
      \Bigl(2^{k}-2k-2\Bigr)\Bigl(\frac12\Bigr)^{k} \\[2mm]
&=\frac13\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr)^{k}
      \bigl(2^{k}-2k-2\bigr) .
\end{aligned}
\]

Compute the two parts separately.

*Sum of \((2/3)^{k}\):*  

\[
\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac23\Bigr)^{k}
 =\frac{(\frac23)^{4}}{1-\frac23}
 =\frac{\frac{16}{81}}{\frac13}= \frac{16}{27}.
\]

*Sum of \((2k+2)(1/3)^{k}\):*  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}(2k+2)\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr)^{k}
&=2\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}k\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr)^{k}
   +2\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr)^{k}  \\
&=2\Bigl(\frac{3}{4}-\frac{2}{3}\Bigr)
   +2\Bigl(\frac32-\frac{40}{27}\Bigr) \\[2mm]
&=2\Bigl(\frac{1}{12}\Bigr)+2\Bigl(\frac{1}{54}\Bigr)
 =\frac{11}{54}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Hence  

\[
\sum_{k=4}^{\infty}\Bigl(\frac13\Bigr)^{k}\bigl(2^{k}-2k-2\bigr)
= \frac{16}{27}-\frac{11}{54}
= \frac{21}{54}= \frac{7}{18}.
\]

Finally  

\[
P(\text{success})=\frac13\cdot\frac{7}{18}= \frac{7}{54}.
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.   Answer to the AIME format  

The probability is \(\displaystyle\frac{7}{54}\); thus \(m=7,\;n=54\).

\[
100m+n = 100\cdot7+54 = 754.
\]

\[
\boxed{754}
\]
